title: What is Calculus?
text:
Calculus provides us with a framework in which we can measure the effects of change and use this to better understand relationships between variables.
There are two main problems we will consider this semester:

title: What is Calculus?
Functions & Their Properties
text: As noted in the course introduction, this semester’s main concepts are tools for understanding relationships between variables. So, before we dive into developing these ideas, we need to have a good understanding of what we mean mathematically by relationships between variables.

title: Functions & Their Properties
text:
Problem 1: Sleep and Productivity






NoteBefore the problem:





Most of the time, we will be interested in relationships where one variable is a function of another. Appropriately, such relationships are called functions.
What criteria does a relationship have to meet in order for it to be a function? Discuss it with your group.

title: Functions & Their Properties
text:
Problem 2: The Pomegranate






NoteBefore the problem:





When trying to understand a function, it is often useful to start by determining its domain and range. Discuss what these terms mean with your group.
Note: In some cases, the domain of a function will be explicitly included as part of the rule defining the function. In other cases, the domain will be implied by the rule or the context in which the rule is given.



A pomegranate is thrown from ground level straight up into the air at time \(t=0\) with an initial velocity of 64 feet per second. The function \(h(t) = -16t^2 + 64t\) gives the pomegranate’s height \(t\) seconds after it was thrown until it hits the ground. Determine the domain and range for the function \(h(t)\).

title: Functions & Their Properties
text:
Problem 3: Matching Rates of Change






NoteBefore the problem:





Recall that we are interested in figuring out ways of measuring change. One simple way to measure change is to calculate the average rate of change of a function over a given interval.
What is the formula for computing average rate of change? What does it tell us about the function? What does it tell us about the graph of the function? Discuss with your group

title: About
text: Currently, this site is maintained by Prof. Kevin Duke at American University. Reach out to Prof. Duke if you find any mistakes or have any questions.

title: Course Notes
text:
During class this semester, we will spend most of our time working on and discussing problems. There will be assigned readings for each class that will help you prepare for these discussions.
Reading mathematics is a skill that is just as essential as doing and communicating mathematics. Class is meant to accompany the reading, not substitute for it. Together, they’ll help you build an initial understanding of concepts and surface the questions worth bringing to class
Make sure you have pencil and paper out when reading and during discussion. Take notes, jot down questions, and try to work through examples on your own before seeing them worked out by others. If you get stuck or have no clue where to start—great! Make a note of it and let’s talk about it.
When you wait for others to solve problems for you, you miss out on all the critical thinking, which can lead to a false sense of understanding. In my experience, you learn far more from actively trying on your own and failing than passively following along and never being wrong.
So, in short, to get the most out of class this semester:

Come prepared!
Be engaged!
Make mistakes!
Ask questions!
